W.P.No.102721/2021 In The Interest Of Justice And Equity.
 This Appeal, Coming On For Preliminary Hearing, This
Day, Vijaykumar A.Patil, J., Made The Following:
 Judgment

This writ appeal is filed assailing the order dated 02.12.2022 passed in W.P.No.102721/2021,
whereby, the learned Single Judge of this Court has refused to interfere with the acquisition proceedings while granting liberty to the appellant/petitioner to file a fresh writ petition challenging declaration if issued rejecting the objections of the petitioner to the acquisition proceedings.

2. The brief facts giving rise to filing of this appeal are that, the appellant/petitioner has filed writ petition seeking prayer to issue writ in the nature of certiorari to quash the impugned Gazette Notification dated NC: 2023:KHC-D:13200-DB 19.03.2020 issued by the respondent No.2 and also Shri A Andaneppa S/O Shivappa Byadagi vs The Principal Secretary on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113584232/
2 set aside the endorsement dated 19.03.2021, which came to be dismissed by the learned Single Judge with a liberty to challenge once the final declaration is issued by the authorities.
3.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Sri. Ramachandra Mali, learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that, the learned Single Judge has committed an error in not appreciating the various provisions of Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Re- settlement Act, 2013 (for short '2013 Act').

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Re- settlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is submitted that, in the instant case, the respondent-authorities have not conducted Social Impact Assessment Study as mandated in 2013 Act.

It is submitted that, Section 4 of the Act, speaks about the preparation of Social Impact Assessment Study and Section 14 provides lapse of social impact assessment report, if the preliminary notification under Section 11 is not issued within twelve months from the date of appraisal of the social impact assessment NC:
2023:KHC-D:13200-DB report submitted by the Expert Group.

It is further submitted that, the authorities are not empowered to issue preliminary notification unless they conduct social impact assessment study and submit the said report, hence the very issuance of preliminary notification under Section 11 which was impugned before the learned Single Judge was in contravention of the various provisions of 2013 Act.

It is also submitted that, Section 6 of the Act speaks about the publication of social impact assessment study and proviso to the said section provides an exemption of conducting social impact assessment study only where the acquisition is for irrigation projects and in the instance case, the acquisition is for the purpose of formation of link road by the authorities, hence, they cannot seek any exemption.
Hence, he seeks to allow the writ appeal by quashing the impugned preliminary notification.

4. Per contra, learned AGA appearing for the respondent supports the impugned order of the learned Single Judge and submits that, the learned Single Judge NC: 2023:KHC-D:13200-DB has taken note of the various provisions of the Act and has rightly dismissed the writ petition holding that there is no cause of action for the petitioners to assail the preliminary notification and it is at the pre-mature stage.

It is further submitted that, similarly placed persons have filed writ petition assailing the very same preliminary notification, wherein, the learned Single Judge of this Court as well as the Division Bench have refused to entertain the challenge to preliminary notification.
Hence, he seeks to dismiss the present writ appeal.

5. Having heard the learned counsel for the appellant, learned AGA and having perused the material on record, it is not in dispute that, the respondent No.2 has issued notification dated 19.03.2022 under Section 11 of the 2013 Act.
On bare perusal of the notification at Annexure-J, it is evident that,
it is only the preliminary notification which was issued by the authority, wherein, they intend to acquire certain extent of land for the public purpose.

It is not in dispute that, pursuant to the said NC: 2023:KHC-D:13200-DB preliminary notification, the authorities have not yet issued any final declaration/final notification to acquire the land in question.
It is not in dispute that, the authorities have served notice on the appellant calling for objection to the preliminary notification.

Admittedly,
the appellant has filed objections to the preliminary notification and raised various grounds on facts as well as on law.

This Court is of the considered view that, the contention of the appellant that the conduct of social impact assessment study is mandatory prior to issuance of preliminary notification and the authority cannot seek exemption of such study, cannot be gone into at this stage in the present proceedings.

The authorities are bound to consider the objections of the appellant before Shri A Andaneppa S/O Shivappa Byadagi vs The Principal Secretary on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/113584232/
3 taking any decision.

entities.text: Shri A Andaneppa S/O Shivappa Byadagi vs The Principal Secretary
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The present proceedings are wholly pre-mature and there is no cause of action for the appellant to initiate the present proceedings, as it is the only intention to acquire the subject land.

We do not find any error in the finding recorded by the learned Single Judge holding that, the writ petition is pre-mature and granting liberty to the appellant to file objections to the notification.
Hence, there is no merit in this appeal calling for any interference by this Court.
7. The Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in Writ Appeal No.100133/2023 disposed of on 28.03.2023 has declined to entertain the challenge to the preliminary notification in question.
Hence, there cannot be any different yardstick to the case on hand.
8. It is made clear that, this Court has not expressed any opinion on the merits and demerits of the case.
It is open for the authorities to consider the objections of the appellant on its merit and in accordance with law.
9. With the above observation, the writ appeal is disposed of.
It is needless to observe that, if the authority proceeds further by issuing final notification, it is always open for the appellant to assail the same in accordance with law.
